questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns you that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: When using roundabouts or traffic circles, you should:

options.text: Slow down as you approach the circle.
Yield to any traffic, pedestrians, or bicyclists already in the circle.
Enter to the right, but steer left in a counterclockwise direction.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach the roundabout. Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians already in the circle. Enter to your right, but steer left so you move around the circle counterclockwise.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles can pass in both directions if it is safe. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign means pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed of oncoming vehicles. They may seem slower than they really are. Make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait to pass until it has passed and you have enough space to change lanes safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use special child seats for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always secure children in a seat with a safety belt.

questions.question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: A motorist making a left turn at an intersection must yield the right-of-way to a bicyclist entering the intersection from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, yield to oncoming bicycles the same way you would yield to oncoming vehicles. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: A traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Get ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
Flash your headlights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Never drive alongside them and never tailgate.

questions.question: Keep extra space ahead of your car when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger car.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Motorcycles are also harder to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the on-ramp to match freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Use your mirrors and check your blind spots to make sure you have space to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be prepared to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to people crossing in a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends. Move to the left lane.
The road curves ahead.
There are intersections coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends. Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to danger ahead. This sign warns that one lane is ending and traffic must move to the left lane.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop and look for oncoming cars before going.
You can go through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is clear. You can turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, let other cars and people in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in an accident?

options.text: Stay near the accident. Move your car to the side of the road if you can.
Report it to police within one week.
Find a phone and call for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay near the accident. Move your car to the side of the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After an accident, stay at the scene. Move your car off the road if possible. Help anyone who is hurt. Call police right away. Share information with other drivers. Report the accident to your insurance company and the DMV.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass only in your direction.
No one can pass in either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass in either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no car from any direction can cross the center line to pass another car.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Increases your ability to react to a hazard.
Often leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to poor driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed causes many crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: When a transit bus signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a transit bus that is signaling to return to the road. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely re-enter traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a traffic signal that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and check for traffic before entering.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to existing traffic.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach with caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when cleared by a flagger, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Only cross when you know no train is coming. Listen carefully and obey any flagger at the crossing.

questions.question: To make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your driving ability. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the turn.
Must stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks must swing wide to complete right turns.

questions.question: Who is subject to the South Carolina Point System?

options.text: Permit holders
All drivers
Intermediate drivers only
Drivers over 65 years of age

questions.correctAnswerText: All drivers
questions.explanation: A driver's license is a privilege, not a right. Your license will be suspended if you get 12 points for violations.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes and carefully pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.
